title: Why Your Brain Loves a Good Story
desc: You forgot a whole presentation by evening, but you remember every second of a friend's three-minute story about a runaway dog. And a book you're not even sure you like is keeping you up past one in the morning. In this calm, sourced, sleep-friendly deep dive we follow one imagined woman, Hana, through a night of one more chapter, as she wonders why stories grip the mind so hard. Along the way we look at what researchers have found about people seeing characters in moving triangles, how the brain explains its own choices with confident stories, why linking words into a story can transform memory, how remembered stories drift and change, how listeners' brains move in step with a storyteller, what it means to be transported into a story and how that can shift beliefs, why a detailed story can feel more likely than a simple one, why spoilers may not spoil anything, what fiction might and might not do for understanding other people, the six basic shapes of stories, the life stories we tell about ourselves, the stories our wandering minds tell all day, and why people around a fire at night tell stories more than anything else. We finish with a few gentle, research-based ideas and then a long, slow guided wind-down to help you fall asleep.
